Hi Sara —

Congrats on the spike this week — I see Olive Analytics crossed the self-serve threshold we track (daily tokens > 250k). That usually means we can unlock some quick wins to reduce per-token latency and avoid billing surprises. Would you have 15 minutes for a short walkthrough where we: 

- Review the traffic pattern that triggered the threshold
- Suggest a lightweight batching/cache tweak that cuts tokens per inference
- Walk through a safety guard (quota alert + fallback) so you don’t hit throttles in peak windows

Quick time options (all PDT):
- Monday 4/14, 10:00–10:15
- Monday 4/14, 15:30–15:45
- Tuesday 4/15, 08:30–08:45

If none of those work, tell me a window that does and I’ll send a calendar invite. Ben (cc) will join the call to capture the action items. I’ve attached a short checklist that shows the one-click changes we usually recommend.

Cheers,

Great — confirmed Monday 4/14 at 15:30 PDT. Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=example-invite-olivemd

Short pre-read answer on batching + latency:
- Small, workload-aware batching (batch size 8–16) tends to reduce per-token CPU time and net latency for throughput-oriented endpoints because of kernel utilization.
- For single-request low-latency paths we keep batch=1; we can configure route-based policies so production critical calls never wait behind batching.
- We’ll show the recommended policy during the 15m call and the expected 95th percentile impact.

Ben will take notes and follow up with the action items + the small config snippet. See attached sample for the mux and batch settings we often apply.

Cheers,
Aditya
